title: RIM Park retrofit grant and Uptown improvement plan
subtitle: Also: new purchasing by-law, Get READI plan, Anndale Road rezoning meeting, Air Force wing lease.
overview: Council approved an application to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities for a $10,000,000 energy and accessibility retrofit at RIM Park {{vote:m6}}. If the grant succeeds, the City would put in $2,000,000 and take on a $6,000,000 loan repaid over 10 years. The work includes replacing old heating and cooling equipment and adding universal washrooms and gender-neutral dressing rooms.

Council approved an updated Uptown Community Improvement Plan {{vote:m8}}, which keeps facade grants and adds grants for accessibility, sustainability and filling vacant commercial space. Council also approved a new by-law setting out how the City buys goods and services, repealing the 2019 by-law {{vote:m5}}. Council approved a lease for 404 K-W Wing (Royal Canadian Air Force Association) at 510 Dutton Dr {{vote:m4}} and accepted the Get READI benchmarking report for information {{vote:m7}}.

Council also held an informal public meeting on a rezoning proposal for 445 Anndale Road. No decision was made, and staff will report back at a later meeting. Council agreed to join the regional all-council meeting on December 19 in Elmira {{vote:m9}}. Council met in closed session on a possible land acquisition or disposition, and the minutes record no public report from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved applying for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities grant for a $10,000,000 RIM Park energy and accessibility retrofit, with $2,000,000 in City funds and a $6,000,000 ten-year loan if the grant is approved.
Council approved the updated plan manual and passed the by-laws designating the project area and adopting the plan.
Council approved a lease with 404 K-W Wing (Royal Canadian Air Force Association) for part of the building at 510 Dutton Dr and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it.
Council accepted for information the report benchmarking the City's equity, diversity and inclusion work against the Get READI plan.
Council approved taking part in a joint meeting of the Region and all area municipalities on December 19, 2025 in Elmira.

debate: On the RIM Park grant, a councillor asked how the work would be paid for if the grant fails. Staff said the City would proceed using its own funding, and that a successful grant could be combined with an earlier federal application.

Asked about gas use at the retrofitted facilities, staff said smaller units would be fully electric. Larger units would be able to switch between electric and gas heating, with gas kept as backup in emergencies.

At the Anndale Road meeting, residents who spoke said they supported more housing in principle. Their concerns were traffic and safety near Lexington Road, too little shared church and visitor parking, the proposed height, privacy next to existing homes, and loss of the community garden.

Residents also questioned whether the green space would be usable for play. Staff said the application meets the landscaped open space minimum and that detailed design comes at site plan stage, while staff are reviewing traffic, servicing and the effect of a later lot split.

Supporters of the Anndale proposal pointed to the need for purpose-built rental and affordable housing, and one speaker asked for better transit frequency in the area. On the Uptown plan, an accessibility delegate welcomed the new grant, and a resident asked for the boundary, unchanged for nearly ten years, to be reconsidered.
